correctness.rationale: The class of finite C3-free oriented graphs freely amalgamates. Permissible one-point types over a path are precisely ternary status words avoiding the unique locally cyclic pair at each path edge. The 3x3 transfer product follows exactly. Exhausting all 128 words of length seven with converse and reversal canonicalization gives 36 classes and 35 distinct polynomials, unique two-class fibre. Independent ternary brute force confirms all ≤6-vertex orientations and both 8-vertex witnesses, including the directional coefficient gap 163 versus 164. Isolated vertex padding multiplies by (1+2z)^k and retains nonisomorphism. No unproved infinite-census assertion.

originality.rationale: The source comparisons concern implication, not title matching: the 2014 archived primary source counts global forbidden-cycle orientations asymptotically, not named-base degree-graded one-types; directed-path homomorphism results treat paths as source and target and do not supply the specific three-state transfer or its sharp collision fibre; generic fixed-target partition functions offer only the method. Relevant published finite-base type work on complete transitive tournament bases cannot imply a path-only threshold because a path has absent nonconsecutive arcs. Targeted published-record searches did not identify a stronger covering theorem; a missing historical computation remains possible.

value.rationale: The complete sharp threshold answers the motivated inverse problem of what information the full adjacency-degree distribution of nonalgebraic one-point types retains about connected path-shaped named bases. The exceptional pair is nonisomorphic even up to converse, has identical complete degree polynomial, but a natural directional refinement separates it. The collision persists for every larger cardinality in the larger forest class. This is a natural finite structural classification, not a coefficient experiment alone; an all-order transfer formula and checkable certificate accompany it.
